script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Thursday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed two point zero two percent down on the session.

Nebius Group reported earnings Thursday and the stock collapsed thirteen point two nine percent. Michael Burry has entered a short position against it. When the man famous for calling the mortgage crisis bets against your holding, the market listens.

The broad market ended lower Thursday, with the Dow snapping a five-session winning streak as investors weighed uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz alongside incoming jobs data that will shape the Federal Reserve's next rate decision. The Nasdaq closed negative on the session, with attention turning toward a cluster of data center and AI infrastructure earnings still ahead.

The top story Thursday belongs to Nebius Group. The stock shed thirteen point two nine percent — the single largest decliner in the portfolio — and the catalyst is layered. Earnings are due imminently, with CoreWeave also reporting in close proximity, putting the entire data center infrastructure space under a microscope. More damaging in the near term is the disclosure that Michael Burry has initiated a short position in Nebius Group. Burry's track record of asymmetric macro calls gives his positioning outsized psychological weight in the market. The short does not invalidate Nebius Group's infrastructure buildout thesis, but it introduces meaningful headline risk and short-side pressure at precisely the moment the company needs its earnings release to serve as a catalyst. Holders should monitor the earnings report closely. Revenue growth and capital deployment pace are the two numbers that matter most.

Applied Optoelectronics was down three point three eight percent on the session despite delivering record second-quarter revenue and returning to non-GAAP profitability for the first time in recent quarters. That marks five consecutive quarters of record revenue. Management noted near-term sales remain constrained by production capacity and component availability — a supply-side ceiling, not a demand problem. Separately, the Federal Communications Commission is drafting a rule that would bar imports of Chinese optical transceivers, which cover more than fifty percent of the global transceiver market. If finalized, that regulatory shift could meaningfully expand the domestic addressable market for Applied Optoelectronics. The earnings print was real. The policy tailwind is forming. Watch for guidance revisions as capacity constraints ease.

Turning to Redwire Corporation, which was the portfolio's standout performer Thursday, up ten point three five percent. Second-quarter revenue grew nearly ninety percent year over year, gross margin hit a record, and the adjusted loss narrowed. Full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed, supported by a record backlog. The seven-day return heading into Thursday's session was already thirty-seven point seven nine percent, per reporting from Yahoo Finance. Aerospace and defense earnings broadly drove a rally in the sector Thursday, with multiple names making bullish technical moves. Redwire remains speculative by analyst characterization, but the fundamental progress is tangible.

AST SpaceMobile was down one point four nine percent Thursday. Separately, a lockup expiration event in the broader space sector — involving nine hundred eleven point five million shares becoming eligible for sale — created float-related anxiety across space-linked names, though that specific event referenced a different issuer. Watch for any spillover sentiment into satellite communications broadly.

Nebius Group, covered in full as the top story, was down thirteen point two nine percent.

Over at Bloom Energy, the stock fell two point two nine percent. The company announced an expanded partnership with MiTAC Computing Technology, deploying fuel cell systems for an islanded microgrid supporting AI infrastructure. The partnership underscores Bloom Energy's positioning as an onsite power provider for data center buildouts — a structural demand driver worth monitoring as AI power consumption continues to scale.

TeraWulf was down two point five two percent Thursday. Bitcoin mining infrastructure names moved in sympathy with broader risk-off sentiment. No company-specific news drove the move. Watch energy cost trends and hashrate data as the next relevant inputs.

Lumentum Holdings was up one point four three percent, the only other primary holding to finish in positive territory alongside Redwire. Lumentum is scheduled to report earnings in close proximity to several other optical and data center names this week, and positioning appears constructive ahead of that print.

IREN Limited was down two point four seven percent. The stock tracked broader weakness in digital infrastructure and Bitcoin-adjacent names. No company-specific catalyst. Sector sentiment remains the primary driver near term.

Sandisk Corporation fell six point eight one percent Thursday — the second-largest decliner in the portfolio. No direct company-specific news drove the move, but memory and storage names faced pressure across the session. Watch for any guidance commentary from adjacent semiconductor reporters.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, Nebius Group's earnings release — revenue growth rate and capital expenditure trajectory are the critical numbers given Michael Burry's short disclosure. Second, Lumentum Holdings' earnings report, which will provide direct visibility into optical component demand across AI data center buildouts. Third, the Friday jobs report, which carries direct implications for Federal Reserve rate path expectations and broad risk appetite heading into next week.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch the Nebius Group earnings release — it is the single event most capable of moving this portfolio's trajectory in either direction.
